rows.stem: The distance between the points \((0, 5)\) and \((-3, 1)\) is :
rows.solution:
By the distance formula, the distance is \(\sqrt{(-3 - 0)^2 + (1 - 5)^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = \sqrt{25} = 5\) units.

This is option (B) 5 units.

rows.subtopic: Trigonometric Ratios of an Acute Angle
rows.solution:
For an acute angle \(\theta\), \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{x}{y}\) means a right triangle with the side opposite \(\theta\) equal to x and the side adjacent to it equal to y. By Pythagoras the hypotenuse is \(\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\).

\(\cos\theta = \dfrac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \dfrac{y}{\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}}\).

This is option (B) \(\dfrac{y}{\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}}\).

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: The zeroes of the polynomial \(3x^2 + 11x - 4\) are :
rows.solution:
Splitting the middle term: \(3x^2 + 11x - 4 = 3x^2 + 12x - x - 4 = 3x(x + 4) - 1(x + 4) = (3x - 1)(x + 4)\).

So the zeroes are \(\dfrac{1}{3}\) and \(-4\). (Check: their sum is \(-\dfrac{11}{3}\) and their product \(-\dfrac{4}{3}\), as \(-\dfrac{b}{a}\) and \(\dfrac{c}{a}\) require.)

This is option (A) \(\dfrac{1}{3}, -4\).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.subtopic: Graphical Method and Nature of Solutions
rows.stem: The point of intersection of the line represented by \(3x - y = 3\) and the y-axis is given by
rows.solution: On the y-axis \(x = 0\), so \(3(0) - y = 3\) and \(y = -3\). The point is \((0, -3)\), which is option (A) \((0, -3)\).

rows.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
rows.stem: If ‘p’ is a root of the quadratic equation \(x^2 - (p + q)\,x + k = 0\), then the value of ‘k’ is
rows.solution:
Since p is a root, it satisfies the equation: \(p^2 - (p + q)p + k = 0\).

\(p^2 - p^2 - pq + k = 0\), so \(k = pq\).

(Equivalently, the sum of the roots is \(p + q\), so the other root is q, and k is the product of the roots, pq.)

This is option (D) \(pq\).

rows.subtopic: Probability from a Collection of Objects
rows.stem: Cards bearing numbers 3 to 20 are placed in a bag and mixed thoroughly. A card is taken out of the bag at random. What is the probability that the number on the card taken out is an even number ?
rows.solution:
The cards bear the numbers 3, 4, ..., 20, so there are \(20 - 3 + 1 = 18\) equally likely cards. The even numbers among them are 4, 6, 8, ..., 20: 9 cards.

\(P(\text{even number}) = \dfrac{9}{18} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), which is option (B) \(\dfrac{1}{2}\).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.subtopic: Consistency from the Ratios of Coefficients
rows.stem: The condition for the system of linear equations \(ax + by = c\); \(lx + my = n\) to have a unique solution is
rows.solution:
The pair \(ax + by = c\) and \(lx + my = n\) has a unique solution when the lines intersect, that is when \(\dfrac{a}{l} \neq \dfrac{b}{m}\).

Cross-multiplying, \(am \neq bl\).

This is option (A) \(am \neq bl\).

rows.subtopic: Section Formula and Ratio of Division
rows.stem: Find the ratio in which the y-axis divides the line segment joining the points \((5, -6)\) and \((-1, -4)\).
rows.solution:
Let the point \(P(0, y)\) on the y-axis divide the segment joining \(A(5, -6)\) and \(B(-1, -4)\) in the ratio \(k : 1\).

Its x-coordinate is \(\dfrac{k(-1) + 1(5)}{k + 1} = \dfrac{-k + 5}{k + 1}\). Since P is on the y-axis, this is 0:

\(-k + 5 = 0\), so \(k = 5\).

The y-axis divides the segment in the ratio \(5 : 1\). (The point of division is \(\left(0, \dfrac{5(-4) + 1(-6)}{6}\right) = \left(0, -\dfrac{13}{3}\right)\).)

rows.subtopic: HCF and LCM by Prime Factorisation
rows.stem: Find the LCM and HCF of 72 and 120
rows.solution:
\(72 = 2^3 \times 3^2\) and \(120 = 2^3 \times 3 \times 5\).

LCM \(= 2^3 \times 3^2 \times 5 = 360\) (the highest power of each prime).

HCF \(= 2^3 \times 3 = 24\) (the lowest power of each common prime).

(Check: \(24 \times 360 = 8640 = 72 \times 120\).)

rows.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
rows.stem: A natural number, when increased by 12, equals 160 times its reciprocal. Find the number.
rows.solution:
Let the natural number be x. Increased by 12 it equals 160 times its reciprocal:

\(x + 12 = \dfrac{160}{x}\), so \(x^2 + 12x = 160\) and \(x^2 + 12x - 160 = 0\).

\((x + 20)(x - 8) = 0\), so \(x = 8\) or \(x = -20\). A natural number cannot be negative, so \(x = 8\).

The number is 8. (Check: \(8 + 12 = 20 = \dfrac{160}{8}\).)

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: If one root of the quadratic equation \(x^2 + 12x - k = 0\) is thrice the other root, then find the value of k.
rows.solution:
Let the roots of \(x^2 + 12x - k = 0\) be \(\alpha\) and \(3\alpha\).

Sum of the roots: \(\alpha + 3\alpha = -12\), so \(4\alpha = -12\) and \(\alpha = -3\).

Product of the roots: \(\alpha \times 3\alpha = -k\), so \(3\alpha^2 = -k\), that is \(3 \times 9 = -k\) and \(k = -27\).

(Check: \(x^2 + 12x + 27 = (x + 3)(x + 9)\), with roots \(-3\) and \(-9\), and \(-9\) is thrice \(-3\).)

rows.subtopic: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
rows.stem: The sum of first seven terms of an A.P. is 182. If its \(4^{\text{th}}\) term and the \(17^{\text{th}}\) term are in the ratio \(1 : 5\), find the A.P.
rows.solution:
Let the first term be a and the common difference d.

\(S_7 = 182\): \(\dfrac{7}{2}(2a + 6d) = 182\), so \(2a + 6d = \dfrac{182 \times 2}{7} = 52\) and \(a + 3d = 26\) ... (i)

\(\dfrac{a_4}{a_{17}} = \dfrac{1}{5}\): \(\dfrac{a + 3d}{a + 16d} = \dfrac{1}{5}\), so \(5a + 15d = a + 16d\) and \(d = 4a\) ... (ii)

Substituting (ii) in (i): \(a + 12a = 26\), so \(a = 2\) and \(d = 8\).

The A.P. is 2, 10, 18, 26, ...

(Check: \(a_4 = 26\) and \(a_{17} = 2 + 16 \times 8 = 130\), in the ratio \(1 : 5\); \(S_7 = \dfrac{7}{2}(4 + 48) = 182\).)

rows.subtopic: Sum of First n Terms of an AP
rows.stem: The sum of first q terms of an A.P. is \(63q - 3q^2\). If its \(p^{\text{th}}\) term is \(-60\), find the value of p. Also, find the \(11^{\text{th}}\) term of this A.P.

rows.subtopic: Number of Tangents from an External Point
rows.stem: Prove that a parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus.
rows.solution:
Let ABCD be a parallelogram whose sides AB, BC, CD and DA touch the circle at P, Q, R and S respectively.

Tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal, so

\(AP = AS\) ... (i), \(BP = BQ\) ... (ii), \(CR = CQ\) ... (iii), \(DR = DS\) ... (iv)

Adding (i) to (iv):

\((AP + BP) + (CR + DR) = (AS + DS) + (BQ + CQ)\), that is \(AB + CD = AD + BC\).

ABCD is a parallelogram, so \(AB = CD\) and \(AD = BC\). Then \(2AB = 2AD\), so \(AB = AD\).

A parallelogram with two adjacent sides equal has all four sides equal (\(AB = CD = AD = BC\)), so ABCD is a rhombus.

rows.subtopic: Number of Tangents from an External Point
rows.stem: In the given figure, tangents PQ and PR are drawn to a circle such that \(\angle RPQ = 30^\circ\). A chord RS is drawn parallel to the tangent PQ. Find the measure of \(\angle RQS\).
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - circle with centre O, tangents PQ (Q at the bottom of the circle) and PR (R at the upper right), the angle at P marked 30 degrees, chord SR across the top parallel to PQ, and chords QS and QR with the angle RQS marked; the stem states every fact used. Page idx 16.
rows.solution:
\(PQ = PR\) (tangents from the external point P), so in triangle PQR the angles opposite them are equal: \(\angle PQR = \angle PRQ = \dfrac{1}{2}(180^\circ - 30^\circ) = 75^\circ\).

Draw QL perpendicular to the tangent PQ at Q, meeting the chord RS at L. A line perpendicular to a tangent at its point of contact passes through the centre O, so QL passes through O.

\(\angle PQL = 90^\circ\), so \(\angle RQL = 90^\circ - \angle PQR = 90^\circ - 75^\circ = 15^\circ\).

\(RS \parallel PQ\) and \(QL \perp PQ\), so \(QL \perp RS\). The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects it, so \(RL = SL\).

In triangles RQL and SQL: \(RL = SL\), \(\angle QLR = \angle QLS = 90^\circ\) and QL is common, so \(\Delta RQL \cong \Delta SQL\) (SAS), and \(\angle SQL = \angle RQL = 15^\circ\).

\(\angle RQS = \angle RQL + \angle SQL = 15^\circ + 15^\circ = 30^\circ\).
